hyps.why: Removing edge 3 hurts far less when edge 5 is a skip, since the 2->3 path then still carries a clean route to the output (IN16 -6 vs -14 to -16).
Upgrading a skip on edge 2 to conv3x3 gives big gains when edge 0 is weak (1x1/skip/pool) but little when edge 0 is already conv3x3.
Upgrading the edge 3 skip to conv3x3 was negative on all datasets when edge 0 was conv3x3, but positive with weaker edge 0 ops.
With edge 3 removed, the output depends on edge 5's path and the skip-to-conv change is very harmful on IN16 (-8).
Replacing avg_pool on edge 4 with conv3x3 was positive on all three datasets only when edge 5 was avg_pool, while IN16 dropped for other edge 5 ops.
Cutting edge 0 is most damaging when the alternative path through edge 1 is only a pooling op (C10 -1.8, IN16 -3.5).
Replacing avg_pool on edge 4 with conv1x1 gave consistent gains on all datasets when edge 0 was a skip, which leaves a parameter-free input path that the new conv complements.
Replacing avg_pool on edge 3 with conv1x1 helped most (C10 +1.76, C100 +2.34, IN16 +2.93) when edge 1 was a skip, and little when edge 1 was none or conv.
With a skip on edge 0, removing edge 4 hurt IN16 badly (-5.7), unlike other edge 0 ops where the effect was small.
Replacing avg_pool on the input edge with conv3x3 gave large, consistent gains on all three datasets (up to +10 IN16).
